transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood Product), Jordan Lee (Seastar Head of Search), Priya Kapoor (Eng Manager), Evan Torres (Data Scientist), Luca Marino (SRE)

Auto-generated summary: Quick demo of embeddings+rerank. Customer curious about latency, cost, and private data handling. Agreed next steps to run pilot and exchange security docs.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll go through a hosted-api demo focusing on embeddings plus rerank, and show the console + Optimize suggestions, feel free to interrupt.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: thanks Maya, quick context — we run a commerce search stack, hybrid vector + lexical, want to improve relevance for variants and user intent, typical queries are short, like 2-6 tokens, and also longer product guides. Main constraints are 150ms p95 and cost targets.
[00:35] Priya Kapoor: and we're on GCP, currently use Elastic for text and a small vector index for certain categories, but maintenance is getting heavy.
[00:47] Liam Patel: got it. High level — Redwood hosted API gives you embeddings endpoint and a rerank endpoint. Typical flow: embed docs -> index; on query embed -> retrieve candidates -> call rerank to score and return top results. We'll demo that flow with a small sample.
[01:05] Evan Torres: curious about KVs and prefix caching — will that help with short queries / session based stuff?
[01:12] Liam Patel: yeah so for conversational or repeated prefixes we do KV cache at the token level — for rerank it's less relevant but for generation latency we see big wins, for embeddings/rerank main levers are batching, model quantization, and using smaller embedding dims for cheaper calls.
[01:30] Maya Chen: I'm going to share my screen and walk through the Console quickstart — show model choices and the rerank endpoint config.
[01:45] [screen share starts] Maya Chen: ok on the Console, under Models you'll see Redwood-embed-4xx (approx) and then the rerank family. You can pin a variant and create a route. Here's an example route: embeddings.v1 -> candidate retrieval (your vector DB) -> rerank.v1 via hosted API.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: what about batching behavior for hosted? If we get spikes during promos, how does that affect tail latency?
[02:20] Liam Patel: hosted autoscaling is per-route, we recommend enabling burst capacity and using our autoscale policy that keeps a warm pool. Optimize will suggest batching sizes based on observed token lengths and throughput — that reduces token cost but we cap batch windows to keep p95 under your SLO.
[02:45] Luca Marino: are there any tenancy concerns? we need data isolation and audit logs for compliance.
[02:51] Samir Rao: good question — hosted keeps customer data logically separated, we provide audit logs via the Console and you can integrate with your SIEM via webhook. For stricter needs we can discuss Dedicated or Private with VPC peering.
[03:10] Priya Kapoor: SOC2? SSO? KMS?
[03:14] Maya Chen: yes SOC2 is available, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported, and KMS integrations for key wrapping. We'll share the SOC2 report and architecture diagram after.
[03:30] [demo continues] Maya Chen: jumping to an example pipeline: here I have a small product dataset (~5k docs) — query -> retrieve top 100 candidates from your vector DB (we recommend 50-200 depending on recall) -> call our rerank endpoint with candidate snippets and the query, rerank returns scores and we apply a threshold. Note you can also do constrained generation or structured output.
[04:00] Priya Kapoor: sending 100 candidates per query sounds expensive — how do you recommend balancing recall vs cost?
[04:10] Liam Patel: common pattern: initial retrieval with approximate neighbor search tuned for recall, then rerank only top N (often 20-50). You can do a two-stage rerank where a smaller cheap reranker filters to 50, then a higher-fidelity model reranks top 10. Optimize can suggest N by simulating cost vs quality on your sample queries.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: what models do you offer for rerank? do you have an ensemble or re-ranking tuned models?
[04:42] Samir Rao: we have several rerankers — lightweight ones (lower cost) for throughput, and larger ones for precision. You can A/B traffic easily through the Console and set automatic fallback to cheaper variants under load.
[05:00] Evan Torres: latency numbers?
[05:03] Liam Patel: from our benchmark on similar workloads — cheap rerankers p95 ~70-120ms for 20 candidates on a hosted route; higher-fidelity models p95 ~180-350ms depending on candidate size and model. We'll provide a benchmark script so you can run on your data.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: ok that helps. Also, is there any on-request caching? sometimes queries repeat within sessions.
[05:31] Liam Patel: you can implement result caching at the app layer, and the Console supports TTL-based caching for specific routes. For embeddings we also support caching at token/embedding level inside a session for low-latency hot-paths.
[05:50] Priya Kapoor: curious about embeddings dimension — we have product titles + attributes, does lower-dim hurt accuracy?
[05:57] Samir Rao: depends — for many commerce scenarios 512 dims are adequate, but we can do 768/1024 for nuance. Optimize will run an evaluation on your prompts and return quality metrics vs cost and recommend quantization profiles.
[06:18] [08:00 into call; demo moves to Console Optimize tab]
[08:05] Maya Chen: here's Optimize — it surfaces suggested batch sizes, cache rules, and quantization candidates for your workload. For example, with your doc length distribution Optimize suggests batch size 16 for embeddings calls and quantize to int8 for embeddings to cut cost ~2.1x while keeping MAP drop <1.5%.
[08:32] Evan Torres: hmm int8 on embeddings, how safe is that?
[08:36] Liam Patel: we've validated on many ecommerce datasets; we'll include the evaluation report. Also you can configure rollouts so only a portion of traffic uses quantized models until you're comfortable.
[08:50] Jordan Lee: what about integration effort — do we have to change our retrieval code much?
[08:55] Maya Chen: minimal; for hosted API you call embeddings endpoint and rerank endpoint via REST/SDK. We have a sample Notebook that shows retrieval+rerank glue code for Python and Node. You plug in your vector DB client to retrieve candidates then call our rerank API.
[09:12] Priya Kapoor: latency from our GCP region to Redwood — do you have regional endpoints?
[09:17] Liam Patel: yes we have multi-region hosted endpoints; your traffic can be routed to the closest region. For strict residency we have Private/VPC deployments.
[09:30] Luca Marino: on logs — can we redact PII before logs leave our environment?
[09:35] Samir Rao: we recommend redacting client-side; also in Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem. For hosted we support configurable data retention windows and field-level masking in logs.
[09:50] [Transcript glitch: Speaker attribution shifts]
[10:02] Speaker 1: so for the demo I have a sample query 'red running shoes size 10' and you can see reranker boosts newer variants higher because of recency signal — we can add signals as features into the rerank request.
[10:22] Jordan Lee: can we include business signals like stock and margin as features?
[10:25] Maya Chen: yes you can pass auxiliary features per candidate in the rerank payload and we will factor them in. We have a feature schema in the docs.
[10:38] Evan Torres: great. Regarding cost — what's ballpark per-call cost for rerank 20 candidates?
[10:44] Liam Patel: depends on model; rough hosted pricing examples — cheap reranker: $0.0009 per call, mid-tier: $0.0035 per call, high-fidelity: $0.01 per call (these are illustrative; we'll send exact pricing). Embeddings cost depends on dims and tokenization.
[11:05] Priya Kapoor: can we run a short pilot with live traffic? we'd like to test on 2 categories with 1% of traffic.
[11:11] Maya Chen: absolutely — typical pilot: 2 weeks, sample dataset, benchmark run, and a small traffic split. We'll set KPIs — p95 latency, CTR lift, and cost per query.
[11:25] Jordan Lee: who needs to be involved from our side?
[11:28] Priya Kapoor: engineering + data science + SRE to validate latency.
[11:33] Maya Chen: noted. We'll also run a quick security Q/A with your security team.
[11:40] Luca Marino: one more — we use customer-managed keys in KMS for some PII encryption, can Redwood integrate?
[11:45] Samir Rao: yes we support bring-your-own-key; we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[11:52] [15:00 mark — deeper technical questions]
[15:03] Evan Torres: about rerank payload size — are there limits on candidate HTML length? our snippets can be large (2-3k chars).
[15:12] Liam Patel: we recommend truncating to relevant fields but we support up to ~8k payload per candidate; cost and latency will increase. For large snippets we often send compressed or pre-processed text (e.g., title+short desc).
[15:35] Jordan Lee: can we do on-prem inference for PII categories only? hybrid mode?
[15:40] Samir Rao: yes — hybrid routing is supported: sensitive requests can be routed to Private nodes while the rest use hosted. It's part of our smart routing policies.
[16:00] Priya Kapoor: demo note — is there a way to do offline evaluation of rerank models with our logs?
[16:06] Liam Patel: Optimize includes an eval harness — you upload labeled pairs or click logs and it runs AUC/MAP/CTR simulations and suggests model candidates and quant profiles. We'll provide sample output.
[16:22] [Crosstalk] Jordan Lee: ok next steps...
[16:28] Maya Chen: quick recap: we'll send security docs, pricing, sample Notebook, and benchmark script. Seastar will share index schema and agree pilot dates.
[16:40] Priya Kapoor: can you share a compact architecture diagram for the pilot?
[16:44] Samir Rao: yes, will attach diagrams to the follow-up email.
[16:50] Jordan Lee: any gotchas around rate limits or burst policies? during holiday promotions we see big bursts.
[16:56] Liam Patel: set route quotas and burst capacity; we can also pre-warm shards for scheduled promotions — for Dedicated customers we reserve GPUs.
[17:12] Evan Torres: will the Console show token-level cost breakdown?
[17:15] Maya Chen: yes, Console has token-level breakdown for generation and call-level cost for embeddings/rerank. You can filter by route/model.
[17:30] Priya Kapoor: do you have references of other commerce customers?
[17:34] Maya Chen: we'll share anonymized case studies and a short list of reference calls; I can hook you up with a PM who did a pilot for a similar retailer.
[17:45] Jordan Lee: timeline — we want to run pilot next week; is that feasible?
[17:49] Maya Chen: yes, we'll target pilot kickoff on 2027-04-14. I'll send calendar invite and materials.
[18:02] [wrap-up and clarifications]
[18:06] Priya Kapoor: one last question — are there throttles per API key? we do per-tenant routing.
[18:12] Liam Patel: we do token-based quotas and per-key rate limits. For pilots we'll set relaxed limits.
[18:25] Maya Chen: great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items discussed.
[18:32] Jordan Lee: thanks all.

End of transcript.
